content.question: In the Dataflow Gen2 authoring experience, what is a data source referred to as before it is loaded to a data store?

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: A team wants to use a Pipeline to first copy/land raw data into the lakehouse, and then use a Dataflow Gen2 to cleanse and curate it into a semantic model. What pattern does this describe?

options.A: It is the only way to apply transformations

options.C: Pipelines are required before any dataflow can be created
options.D: Dataflows cannot be run on their own

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Ingest Data with Dataflows Gen2 in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: Your organization has several Power BI report authors who all need a standardized, cleaned "Date" dimension table, and you want to avoid each of them re-building their own date logic. Which approach best fits the benefits described for Dataflows Gen2?

options.B: Use only a pipeline with a Copy Data activity — no transformation needed

options.D: Use KQL to perform both the transformation and the stored procedure execution

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: What is the primary purpose of the bronze layer in a medallion architecture?

options.A: To model data as a star schema for reporting
options.B: To serve as the raw landing zone for data, unmodified from the source
options.D: To store only aggregated summary data

content.explanation: Bronze stores structured, semi-structured, or unstructured data exactly as it arrives — no changes, no cleanup, intentionally.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Which layer is typically modeled as a star schema for business consumption?
content.explanation: Gold is where data is modeled for business use, typically as a star schema with facts and dimensions, ready for reports, models, and dashboards.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: What kind of activities are typical in the silver layer?

options.A: Raw ingestion only, with no changes
options.B: Combining/merging sources and enforcing data quality (removing nulls, deduplication)

content.explanation: Silver focuses on validation and refinement — standardizing formats, deduplicating, and joining bronze sources into one consistent, integrated dataset.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Why is bronze layer data kept in its original, unmodified format?

options.B: So you can reprocess from bronze if a downstream transformation goes wrong, without returning to the source system
options.C: Because Fabric doesn't allow transformation of raw files

content.explanation: Keeping bronze raw and untouched is a deliberate safety net — it's your recovery point if something breaks further downstream.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Is the three-layer bronze/silver/gold pattern a strict, fixed requirement?

options.A: Yes, exactly three layers must always be used
options.B: No — it's a starting point; you can add layers like a landing zone or domain-specific layers as needed
options.C: No, only two layers are ever needed
options.D: Yes, and the layer names must be bronze/silver/gold exactly

content.explanation: The module is explicit that the names and number of layers are flexible — what matters is that each layer has a clear purpose and audience.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: When structuring a lakehouse for medallion architecture, what does using a single lakehouse with schemas (bronze/silver/gold) offer compared to separate lakehouses/workspaces?

options.B: Simpler management, better suited to smaller teams or early-stage projects
options.C: The ability to assign different capacities per layer

content.explanation: A single lakehouse with bronze/silver/gold schemas trades some isolation for lower management overhead — a good fit when you don't yet need separate permissions or capacity per layer.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Which approach provides the strongest isolation between medallion layers, appropriate for regulatory or compliance scenarios?
content.explanation: This gives each layer its own capacity, role assignments, and clear ownership boundary — the strongest isolation option, required for regulatory or compliance scenarios, at the cost of more workspaces to manage.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: If your source data already lives in cloud storage like OneLake, ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3, or Google Cloud Storage, what's the recommended way to bring it into the bronze layer?

options.B: Use a OneLake shortcut to reference it without copying
options.C: Manually download and re-upload the files
options.D: Convert it to Delta format before ingestion

content.explanation: Shortcuts keep bronze in sync with the source automatically, with no pipeline or ingestion code needed — but only when the source is already in supported cloud storage. Other sources still need pipelines, dataflows, or notebooks.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Which silver-layer transformation tool lets you write a SQL query that Fabric automatically keeps up to date — updating only changed rows as new bronze data arrives — without scheduling anything?
content.explanation: You describe the target table with a SQL query, and Fabric creates and maintains it — updating only changed rows as new bronze data arrives, with no manual scheduling.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: What is the key difference between a materialized lake view and a regular SQL view?

options.A: A regular view saves results as a real table; a materialized lake view reruns its query every time
options.B: A materialized lake view saves the results as a real table and updates incrementally; a regular view reruns its query every time it's queried
options.C: There is no functional difference between them
options.D: Materialized lake views only work on the gold layer

content.explanation: This distinction is the core value proposition: materialized lake views trade some flexibility for performance and automatic freshness, powered by Delta's change tracking.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: What is the tradeoff of using a materialized lake view for a silver-layer transformation?

options.B: The transformation must be expressible as SQL; Python logic requires a notebook instead
options.C: It only works with unstructured data

content.explanation: This is the explicit tradeoff called out in the module — materialized lake views are SQL-only, so anything needing Python-based logic has to go through a notebook.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Which silver/gold transformation tool is best suited for large datasets, complex logic, custom calculations, or API calls that a dataflow can't handle?
content.explanation: They give full control using Python or SQL, making them the right tool for large datasets, complex logic, custom calculations, or API calls — things dataflows and materialized lake views can't handle.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: How does a data science team's gold layer commonly differ in shape from a finance team's gold layer, even when built from the same silver data?

options.A: They can't differ — gold layer shape is fixed once defined
options.B: A data science team might want a flat, wide table for feature engineering, while finance might want pre-aggregated summaries
options.C: Data science teams cannot access the gold layer
options.D: Finance teams always require a star schema, and data science teams never do

content.explanation: The module explicitly notes you can have multiple gold layers from the same silver data, each modeled differently for different audiences' needs.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Besides a lakehouse, what other Fabric item can serve as the gold layer for teams that primarily work in SQL?
content.explanation: For SQL-first teams, a Data Warehouse can serve as the gold layer instead of a lakehouse — same layer purpose, different underlying item type.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: True or false? The SQL analytics endpoint operates in read-only mode over lakehouse Delta tables.
content.explanation: The SQL analytics endpoint gives direct T-SQL access to gold layer data, but strictly in read-only mode — you can query, create views/functions, and apply SQL security, but not modify the underlying Delta tables.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: True or false? Power BI semantic models connecting to the gold layer via Direct Lake mode require a separate manual refresh step to show current data.
content.explanation: Direct Lake reads directly from the Delta files in OneLake instead of importing a copy, so reports always reflect current data — no separate refresh step required.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: True or false? Every Fabric lakehouse comes with a built-in DefaultReader role that grants all ReadAll users access to all data by default.
content.explanation: Every lakehouse comes with a built-in DefaultReader role granting all ReadAll users access to all data by default; you have to modify or delete it if you want to restrict that default access.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: True or false? OneLake data access roles require putting each medallion layer in a separate workspace in order to function. ---
content.explanation: OneLake data access roles are specifically the alternative to separate workspaces — they give granular, table/folder-scoped control within a single lakehouse, exactly for teams sharing a workspace who need different access per layer.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: Your organization shares a single workspace across teams, but you need gold layer consumers to query gold tables while being blocked from seeing bronze or silver data — without creating separate workspaces. What should you configure?

options.A: Workspace-level Admin role for gold consumers
options.B: A OneLake data access role scoped to the gold tables/folders

content.explanation: This is exactly the described use case: granular per-layer access within one shared workspace, without the overhead of separate workspaces. A workspace-level Admin role (A) would be far too broad and wouldn't restrict visibility by layer at all.

topic: Organize a Fabric lakehouse using medallion architecture design

content.question: A transformation change to your silver layer notebook accidentally corrupts downstream data, and you need to quickly revert to the previous known-good version of that notebook. What Fabric capability directly supports this recovery scenario?

options.B: Git integration, allowing you to revert to a previous commit

content.explanation: Fabric's Git integration versions notebooks, pipelines, and lakehouse definitions together, so a bad transformation change can be rolled back to the last known-good commit — exactly the recovery scenario described.

topic: Orchestrate processes and data movement with Microsoft Fabric

topic: Orchestrate processes and data movement with Microsoft Fabric

options.A: Applying complex transformations while merging multiple sources
options.B: Copying data directly between a supported source and destination with no transformation

content.question: Before running a pipeline, what option can you use to check that its configuration is correct?

content.question: Where can you view the run history of a pipeline?

options.A: Only from the Fabric admin portal

content.question: Your data needs light transformation and merging from two different sources as it's ingested into the lakehouse, with no need for further Spark processing afterward. What's the most appropriate single-activity approach?

options.A: Copy Data activity, since it supports all transformation types
options.B: Data Flow activity referencing a Dataflow Gen2 with the transformation/merge logic built in
options.D: Delete data activity followed by manual reload

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What is a Spark pool in Microsoft Fabric?

options.A: A single virtual machine dedicated to one notebook
options.B: A cluster of compute nodes that distribute data processing tasks

options.D: A destination type for a Dataflow Gen2

content.question: In a Spark pool's architecture, which node coordinates distributed processes through a driver program?

content.question: What is the purpose of the "starter pool" provided in every Fabric workspace?

options.A: It's a training sandbox with no real data access
options.B: It enables Spark jobs to start and run quickly with minimal setup
options.C: It's only used for Spark job definitions, never notebooks

content.explanation: Every Fabric workspace gets a starter pool by default, configurable to your workload/cost needs; custom pools are optional additions, not replacements.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: Which Spark pool configuration setting controls whether nodes are automatically provisioned as needed (and the min/max node count)?

content.question: What does "dynamic allocation" specifically control in a Spark pool?

options.A: Which virtual machine type is used for nodes
options.B: Whether executor processes on worker nodes scale based on data volume

options.A: A vectorized processing engine that improves performance on large Parquet/Delta datasets
options.B: It manages user authentication for Spark pools
options.C: It eliminates the need for a Spark pool
options.D: It converts PySpark code into T-SQL automatically

content.explanation: It runs Spark operations directly on lakehouse infrastructure for significant performance gains on those formats.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What does high concurrency mode allow multiple users or processes to do?

options.A: Edit the exact same notebook cell simultaneously
options.B: Share a Spark session for efficient resource use, while keeping code execution isolated

content.question: What does a Spark runtime determine, as distinct from an environment?

options.A: Which libraries a user has manually installed
options.B: The version of Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Python, and other core components

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: When should you use a Spark job definition rather than a notebook?

options.A: When you want to interactively explore data with immediate visual feedback
options.B: When you want to run Spark code as an automated, on-demand or scheduled process
options.C: When you only need markdown documentation, no code
options.D: When you want to avoid using PySpark entirely

content.explanation: Notebooks are for interactive exploration; Spark job definitions are for automated script execution.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What is a key benefit of specifying an explicit schema when loading a dataframe (versus letting Spark infer it)?

options.A: It's the only way Spark can read a CSV file
options.B: It improves performance and is useful when column headers aren't present in the source file
options.D: It converts the data to Delta format

content.explanation: The module states this explicitly — plus it's necessary when there's no header row to infer column names from.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: Which file format is preferred in Microsoft Fabric for Spark tables, due to support for transactions, versioning, and streaming data?

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Deleting a managed table in the Spark catalog also deletes its underlying data.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? A temporary view created with createOrReplaceTempView persists permanently across all future Spark sessions.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Matplotlib can plot directly from a Spark dataframe without any conversion.
content.explanation: Matplotlib requires data in a Pandas dataframe, not a Spark dataframe — you need to call .toPandas() to convert it first before charting.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Partitioning a saved dataframe (e.g., with partitionBy) can improve query performance by reducing unnecessary disk I/O when filtering. ---
content.explanation: Partitioning is explicitly called out as an optimization technique that reduces unnecessary disk I/O when queries filter on the partitioning column, improving performance across worker nodes.

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: You want multiple data analysts to interactively explore a dataset, mixing markdown commentary with executable code cells, and see results immediately as they iterate. What's the best tool for this?

options.B: A notebook combining markdown and executable code cells

topic: Use Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: You have a CSV file with no header row containing product data, and you want correct data types and the best possible load performance — without relying entirely on Spark's automatic inference. What should you do?

options.B: Query data from external KQL databases as if stored locally, without copying it

options.A: Deletes the data from the eventhouse

options.C: Converts the database into a Lakehouse

content.question: Which operator is used to select specific columns from a table, reducing the data processed downstream?

content.question: According to the module's optimization guidance, how should filters be ordered in a query for best performance?

options.B: Put filters that eliminate the most data first

content.explanation: Think funnel: broad, high-impact filters (like a time range) go first, narrower filters follow, minimizing the data volume as early as possible.

content.question: When performing a join in KQL, which table should be placed first for best performance?

options.C: It doesn't matter which table is first

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What are materialized views designed to solve?

options.B: The performance challenge of repeatedly recalculating aggregations across massive datasets

options.D: Security and access control for KQL databases

options.D: A Lakehouse shortcut and a Warehouse table

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Querying a materialized view always returns only the precomputed data as of the last background update, ignoring any newer data.
content.explanation: Materialized views combine the materialized part and the delta at query time, so they always return fresh, up-to-date results — not stale data frozen at the last background update.

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? KQL databases can ingest data from sources like Azure Event Hubs, Fabric Eventstream, and Apache Kafka connectors.

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Reducing the number of columns selected (projecting early) has no effect on KQL query performance. ---

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

topic: Work with real-time data in an Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What is OneLake in Microsoft Fabric?

options.B: Fabric's centralized data storage architecture built on ADLS Gen2

topic: Introduction to end-to-end analytics using Microsoft Fabric

options.B: To reference files or storage locations without copying the data

options.B: A single physical server dedicated to one user
options.C: A billing unit only, with no access control function

content.question: Where is Fabric administration centralized?

content.question: What does the OneLake catalog help you do?

topic: Introduction to end-to-end analytics using Microsoft Fabric

content.question: Which role can enable Microsoft Fabric for an organization via implicit, organization-wide permissions?

content.question: According to the module, which persona curates data assets in lakehouses, ensures data quality, and creates semantic models to enable self-service analytics?

content.explanation: Delta Lake maintains a transaction log specifically so you can query previous versions of the data or roll back changes when needed.

content.question: When you create a new lakehouse, what happens with schemas by default?

options.A: Schemas are disabled until manually enabled
options.B: Schemas are enabled by default, with a "dbo" schema created automatically

options.D: Schemas only apply to the Files folder

content.question: What are the two components stored for each Delta table in a lakehouse?

content.question: Which of the four ACID properties ensures that concurrent, in-process transactions can't interfere with one another?

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What happens when you delete a managed table from the lakehouse metastore?

options.A: Only the metadata is removed; underlying files remain
options.B: Both the table definition and the underlying data files are deleted
options.C: Nothing happens until VACUUM is run
options.D: The table is converted to an external table automatically

content.explanation: This is the defining trait of a managed table — metastore and files are tied together.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What happens when you delete an external table from the lakehouse metastore?

options.A: The metadata definition is removed, but the underlying data files are NOT deleted
options.B: Both metadata and data files are deleted
options.C: It cannot be deleted, only overwritten

content.explanation: External tables only map the metastore definition to a separate storage location; deleting the table leaves the actual files untouched.

content.question: Which API lets you define a delta table's schema and columns directly in Spark code, without first loading a dataframe?
content.explanation: This lets you specify a table name and add columns directly in code (e.g., DeltaTable.create(spark).tableName(...).addColumn(...)) without needing an existing dataframe.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What is the "small file problem" in Delta Lake / Spark?

options.A: Too few files, causing slow writes
options.B: Many small files accumulating from updates and deletes, slowing down queries
options.C: Files that are too large to fit in memory

content.explanation: Because Parquet files are immutable, every update or delete writes a new file — over time this produces a large number of small files that degrade query performance.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What does the OptimizeWrite feature do, and is it enabled by default in Fabric?

options.A: Consolidates existing files on a schedule; disabled by default
options.B: Writes fewer, larger files as data is written; enabled by default
options.C: Deletes old Parquet files; disabled by default
options.D: Partitions tables automatically; enabled by default

content.explanation: OptimizeWrite acts at write time to prevent the small file problem before it starts, and it's on by default in Fabric (though it can be toggled at the session, table property, or command level).

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What does the OPTIMIZE command do, as distinct from OptimizeWrite?

options.A: It runs as data is being written, preventing small files from forming in the first place
options.B: It's a table maintenance feature that consolidates existing small Parquet files into fewer, larger ones after the fact
options.C: It removes old data files beyond a retention period
options.D: It partitions a table by a specified column

content.explanation: Unlike OptimizeWrite (which prevents small files during writes), OPTIMIZE is run afterward to clean up files that have already accumulated.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What does V-Order do, and what's the trade-off of using it?

options.A: It speeds up writes but slows down reads
options.B: It speeds up reads (especially via Power BI/SQL Verti-Scan) at the cost of roughly 15% slower writes
options.C: It compresses data losslessly with no performance trade-offs at all
options.D: It only works with external tables

content.explanation: V-Order applies special sorting, encoding, and compression to Parquet files, trading some write speed for meaningfully faster reads across Fabric's compute engines.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What does the VACUUM command do?

options.A: Compacts small files into larger ones
options.B: Permanently removes old, unreferenced Parquet data files older than the retention period

content.explanation: VACUUM cleans up files left behind by updates/deletes that are no longer needed for time travel within the retention window — but it does not touch the transaction log itself.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: What is the default — and minimum allowed — retention period for VACUUM in Microsoft Fabric?

options.B: 7 days (168 hours), and the system prevents a shorter period
options.C: 30 days, with no way to change it

content.explanation: This default protects your ability to time travel; you can't set VACUUM to a shorter retention window than this.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: When should you avoid partitioning a Delta table, per the module's guidance?

options.A: When you have very large amounts of data
options.B: When the partitioning column has high cardinality, creating a large number of partitions
options.C: When tables can be split into a few large partitions
options.D: When you want to enable data skipping

content.explanation: This (along with small data volumes generally) can make the small file problem worse rather than improving performance — partitioning works best on very large datasets split into a few large partitions.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Running VACUUM also deletes the transaction log entries associated with the removed files.
content.explanation: VACUUM removes old data files only — it doesn't touch the transaction log. In fact, VACUUM itself commits an entry to the transaction log, which is why you can see previous VACUUM runs via DESCRIBE HISTORY.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? You can retrieve an earlier version of a Delta table's data by specifying a versionAsOf or timestampAsOf option when reading it.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? When using a Delta table as a Spark Structured Streaming source, data modifications (updates/deletes) are allowed by default without any special configuration.
content.explanation: By default, only append operations are allowed when a Delta table is used as a streaming source — modifications (updates/deletes) cause an error unless you explicitly specify the ignoreChanges or ignoreDeletes option.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: True or false? Spark processes streaming data using a completely different API from batch data, requiring entirely separate code. ---
content.explanation: Spark processes both streaming and batch data using the same API — Structured Streaming is based on a "boundless dataframe" concept, meaning the same general dataframe operations apply to both.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: You need to permanently free up storage by removing old Parquet files that are no longer referenced and are older than your compliance-mandated retention window, while still being able to view table history via DESCRIBE HISTORY. What should you run?
content.explanation: This directly matches the described need: permanently remove old unreferenced data files past a retention threshold. Table history remains visible via DESCRIBE HISTORY because VACUUM doesn't touch the transaction log — only OPTIMIZE (A) consolidates files rather than deleting them, so it wouldn't free storage the same way.

topic: Work with Delta Lake tables in Microsoft Fabric

content.question: You're staging raw data that will only be read once or twice before being discarded, and you want to minimize write overhead. What should you consider doing regarding V-Order?

options.A: Enable V-Order to maximize read speed regardless of write cost
options.B: Disable V-Order, since the read benefit doesn't offset the write overhead for write-intensive, rarely-read staging data
options.C: V-Order cannot be disabled once enabled
options.D: Use partitioning instead of V-Order for staging data

content.explanation: The module explicitly calls this out: V-Order's ~15% write overhead isn't worth it when data is only read once or twice, so disabling it can reduce overall ingestion processing time in staging scenarios.
